support_records.excerpt:
Additional parts of the standard library are shipped as separate libraries. These include:

- `scala.reflect` - Scala's reflection API (scala-reflect.jar)
- `scala.xml` - XML parsing, manipulation, and serialization (scala-xml.jar)
- `scala.collection.parallel` - Parallel collections (scala-parallel-collections.jar)
- `scala.util.parsing` - Parser combinators (scala-parser-combinators.jar)
- `scala.swing` - A convenient wrapper around Java's GUI framework called Swing (scala-swing.jar)

####  Automatic imports
Identifiers in the scala package and the `scala.Predef` object are always in scope by default.

Some of these identifiers are type aliases provided as shortcuts to commonly used classes. For example, `List` is an alias for
`scala.collection.immutable.List`.

Other aliases refer to classes provided by the underlying platform. For example, on the JVM, `String` is an alias for `java.lang.String`.

-    package scala

Core Scala types.

skill_specs.name: Resolve Scala Standard Library Module Import
skill_specs.description: Locate and import optional Scala standard library modules (reflect, xml, collection.parallel, util.parsing, swing) by their canonical package names and corresponding JAR artifacts.
skill_specs.skill_body:
When your code requires functionality from optional Scala libraries, identify the module by its use case, then declare the correct import statement and ensure the corresponding JAR is available in your build classpath.

## Objective

correctly identify and import the required optional Scala library module
## Applicable Signals

- code needs reflection API
- code needs XML handling
- code needs parallel collections
- code needs parser combinators
- code needs Swing GUI bindings

## Contraindications

- the required functionality is already in core scala package or java.lang
- the JAR is not available in the build classpath

## Workflow Steps

- Identify the functional requirement (reflection, XML, parallel collections, parsing, or GUI).
- Map the requirement to the corresponding optional module: scala.reflect, scala.xml, scala.collection.parallel, scala.util.parsing, or scala.swing.
- Declare the import statement using the canonical package name (e.g., `import scala.reflect._`).
- Ensure the corresponding JAR (e.g., scala-reflect.jar, scala-xml.jar) is declared in build configuration.

## Output Contract

- correct import statement and JAR dependency declared in build configuration
- downstream code can reference the imported module without resolution errors

skill_specs.name: Resolve Scala Automatic Scope Availability
skill_specs.description: Reference canonical knowledge about automatic availability of identifiers from scala package and scala.Predef in Scala code without explicit import statements. Use when debugging unresolved identifier errors, understanding default namespace behavior, or documenting which core identifiers are automatically in scope.
skill_specs.skill_body:
Scala automatically makes all identifiers in the scala package and scala.Predef object available in scope by default. This means you can use core Scala types, functions, and utilities without writing explicit import statements. When troubleshooting identifier resolution errors, check whether the identifier belongs to scala.* or scala.Predef before adding imports. Separately shipped libraries (scala-reflect.jar, scala-xml.jar, scala-parallel-collections.jar, scala-parser-combinators.jar, scala-swing.jar) require explicit dependency and import declarations.

## Objective

Reference automatic import behavior for core Scala identifiers and distinguish from separately shipped libraries
## Applicable Signals

- Unresolved identifier error during compilation
- Question about implicit imports in Scala
- Need to document default namespace availability
- Debugging missing import statements

## Contraindications

- Generating explicit import statements
- Handling package shadowing or name conflicts
- Configuring custom predef or alternative standard library
- Working with non-standard Scala environments

## Constraints

- Applies only to scala.* and scala.Predef identifiers
- Does not cover separately shipped libraries (scala.reflect, scala.xml, scala.swing, scala.util.parsing, scala.collection.parallel)
- Automatic scope is standard Scala behavior; custom configurations may override

## Cautions

- Separately shipped libraries (scala-reflect.jar, scala-xml.jar, scala-parallel-collections.jar, scala-parser-combinators.jar, scala-swing.jar) require explicit dependency and import declarations
- Name shadowing or local redefinition can override automatic scope

## Output Contract

- Confirmation that scala.* and scala.Predef identifiers are available without explicit import statement
- Clarity on which identifiers are automatically in scope versus which require explicit dependency or import
- Distinction between core automatic scope and separately shipped libraries requiring explicit imports
